brief: Ian reviewed the preview and questioned whether the Grenze 'Latest issues' heading helps wayfinding or just asks the reader to decipher blackletter. Reverted, and derived an explicit rule for where Grenze belongs across DL.
rule: Grenze Gotisch is scoped to first-glance brand-identity moments only — text that is recognized once per session, not scanned or read under time pressure. It does not belong on functional/navigational text that identifies content or is scanned repeatedly.
grenzeRoles: Homepage hero H1 (once per homepage visit, the biggest identity statement on the site)
explicitlyNotGrenze: Homepage 'Latest issues' index heading — reverted from Grenze back to upright Source Serif (also fixed a pre-existing italic-heading purity violation in the same rule)
Newsletter issue H1s (e.g. 'DL 438') — functional, per-issue, scanned every read; correctly untouched
Newsletter archive H1 ('Digitally Literate' on /newsletter/) — a utility/working page, not a first-glance identity moment; deliberately left Source Serif
Ordinary note/Evergreen/Grove titles, H2/H3 section heads, mono metadata, blockquote emphasis — untouched, all correct as-is
openQuestion: Whether the footer wordmark ('/ Digitally Literate') should move to Grenze under this same rule — it's brand-identity text, not functional, but was explicitly out of scope in the original handoff. Not changed pending Ian's call.

brief: Hallmark audit pass on design/grenze-gotisch-identity: checked Grenze consistency across DL, fixed font-hosting drift
fixed: Font-hosting drift: Source Serif 4 / Inter / JetBrains Mono were still loading from a Google Fonts @import in custom-style.scss even though self-hosted files already existed unused in src/site/fonts/. Added @font-face for all three (normal + Source Serif italic) in tokens.css and removed the Google Fonts @import — one self-hosting strategy for all four typefaces (incl. Grenze), zero external font network dependency.

Ian's call: .garden-index h2 ('Latest issues' homepage section heading) moved to --garden-font-identity, upright at weight 500, matching the hero — the one additional display role the original handoff allowed.
Ian's call: deleted the two unused committed font files (Inter-Italic, JetBrainsMono-Italic) — nothing in the design referenced them.

identityTest: Grenze Gotisch (self-hosted OFL) via new --garden-font-identity token
scope: masthead wordmark + homepage hero H1 only; reading/UI/mono roles unchanged
brief: Grenze Gotisch identity-layer test on digitallyliterate.net, branch design/grenze-gotisch-identity
decisions: Grenze Gotisch has no italic instance upstream; the homepage hero H1 goes upright (font-style: normal) instead of a synthesized faux-italic slant on a blackletter face.
Weight held at 500 for both masthead and hero, per the decision record that weight 600 reads as overtly gothic.
Ordinary post titles (e.g. DL issue H1s), the newsletter archive H1, and the footer wordmark stay in Source Serif 4 — Grenze is an identity-layer accent, not the reading voice.
No design.md emitted; vault design contract remains authoritative pending Ian's review of the draft PR.

brief: Digitally Literate newsletter and curated public notebook
decisions: Public note types are Evergreen, Grove, and Forest.
Seed, Sprout, and Plant remain private development states.
Light mode is the default reading surface; explicit reader choice persists.
Texture is limited to semantic Apparatus regmarks, never resting-state backgrounds or body text.
Homepage rhythm uses a compact named spacing scale and avoids inherited plugin block margins.
Homepage illustration is a decorative grove, not a maturity-stage taxonomy mark.
The masthead retains the full Digitally Literate name.
The homepage title remains on one line while the earlier geometric grove form supplies the counterweight.
Evergreen motion is isolated to the tree forms; the grove baseline remains fixed.
